newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronist leads key Buenos Aires Congress poll.
newsitem.headline: Peronist leads key Buenos Aires Congress poll.

text.p: The candidate of the ruling Peronist Party for the key seat of Buenos Aires province held a clear lead in a poll of voter intentions for October congressional elections published Tuesday.

Hilda Duhalde, wife of Buenos Aires province Gov. Eduardo Duhalde, had the support of 35.9 percent of voters, according to the survey by private pollsters Ricardo Rouvier y Asociados printed in the La Nacion daily newspaper.
In second place with 26.9 percent was Sen. Graciela Fernandez Meijide of the center-left Frepaso alliance.
Former President Raul Alfonsin of the Radical Party was third, with 18.6 percent.
Some 13.5 percent said they still did not know who they would vote for. The remaining 5.1 percent supported other candidates.
Buenos Aires province, which does not include the center of the city of Buenos Aires, is home to 40 percent of the voters in Argentina.
The poll of 1,470 people was taken from May 12-24, coinciding with violent clashes between protesters calling for jobs and police in the poor northwestern province of Jujuy.
La Nacion did not give a margin of error.
